notes:
Background: mid-market SaaS (product analytics) building an in-app assistant + search/rerank layer. Started with Redwood Hosted API trial in Jan 2025 to validate latency and UX. Trial ran across product and support teams (14-day trial).

POC highlights: average request profile: 1) support chat (50% of calls) average prompt 90 tokens, average completion 240 tokens; 2) product search/rerank (30%) mostly embeddings + rerank calls (average embedding size 768, avg tokens returned 40); 3) summarization / batch jobs (20%) long-context summarization (avg input 1200 tokens, output ~200 tokens).

Traffic observed during hosted trial: baseline 3 QPS, peak bursts up to 18 QPS (short spikes). Production forecast from product team (Q2 launch): steady-state 80-120 QPS, expected peak bursts 250-400 QPS during feature launches. Concurrency target: 50-120 concurrent streams depending on user session model. Token mix estimate for prod: ~70% generation tokens, 30% embedding/rerank tokens by cost-weighted units.

Hosted trial metrics: median latency (text-gen) 90-140ms for short prompts; p95 420-680ms during peak events. Embeddings p50 ~35ms, p95 ~120ms. Cost sensitivity: target < $0.08 / active user per month at projected scale; finance flagged current hosted unit costs as too high without batching/caching optimizations.

Customer asks: dedicated reserved pool for predictable throughput and data isolation; ability to pin model versions and run canary rollouts; routing policies to fallback to smaller model when capacity constrained; auditing + KMS integration; residency in us-east required for compliance. Quote request includes 12-month committed capacity with burst credits.

Direct quote from Head of Product: "We need predictable latency at scale — p95 under 250ms for short-turn chat otherwise product UX suffers. Also need clear pricing for committed capacity vs burst usage."

Security / procurement: running internal SOC2 checklist; legal asked for data-residency and audit log samples; security team wants KMS + DoD/retention policy details. Procurement lead expects procurement sign-off timeline ~6-8 weeks once sizing and SOW are final.

Redwood team notes: suggested optimizations — prefix/KV caching for repeated flows (could cut token cost ~15-25%), workload-aware batching during off-peak, quantized smaller variant for fallback. Initial dedicated sizing recommendation below (work-in-progress):
- Starting configuration: 4 x H100-equivalent workers for steady 100 QPS gen with concurrency ~60 (model: 2-4B quantized variant for default, 13B for high-quality route).
- Burst plan: allow autoscale to an additional 2-4 workers for short spikes to reach 300-400 QPS for up to 15 minutes; include burst credits in pricing proposal.
- Estimated monthly token volume: 1.8B generation tokens + 0.6B embedding-related tokens (embeddings counted separately).

Open items: final model choices for production (latency vs. quality tradeoff), confirmation of residency + KMS architecture, procurement approval of commit level, SLA targets (p95 latency and uptime), legal on indemnity.

Next immediate actions: 1) hand off dedicated sizing workbook to finance + infra (Deliver 2025-02-21). 2) Diego to run a short stress-run on Redwood Dedicated staging to validate concurrency targets (week of 2025-02-17). 3) Schedule procurement / legal workshop (2025-02-25).
